expectations.text: States that the published error-budget and SLO literature is written consumer-side, for a team measuring its own dependence on someone else's API, and does not transfer wholesale to a provider publishing numbers for partners
expectations.evidence: "the literature... is written for a team measuring its own dependence on someone else's API."

expectations.text: Rejects presenting the multi-vendor multiplicative availability argument to Marrowpoint's partners, because that arithmetic describes the consumer's position rather than Marrowpoint's
expectations.evidence: "The multi-vendor message is the wrong direction... does not transfer to the provider side."

expectations.text: Warns that an integration measurement includes the partner's own code and their customers' configuration, so committing to a number derived from it is a promise Marrowpoint only partly controls
expectations.evidence: "The measurement includes the partner's own code and their customers' configs, so you'd be promising something you only partly control."

expectations.text: Routes formal SLA and uptime publication to a separate status-and-incident-communication scope rather than deriving it from the integration health view
expectations.evidence: "Formal SLA or uptime publication belongs to... api-status-communication."

expectations.text: Keeps per-integration and per-endpoint granularity as a part that does transfer, against a single blended platform number
expectations.evidence: "Use per-endpoint SLIs, not one blended number. This part of the SRE literature does transfer."

expectations.text: Keeps multi-window burn-rate detection as a part that does transfer: a long window confirming the problem is sustained plus a short window confirming it is still active
expectations.evidence: "multi-window burn-rate alerting: a short window for sudden breaks, a long window for slow degradation."

expectations.text: States that nothing in the published record establishes what a provider-side integration SLO should contain
expectations.evidence: "Nothing in the published record defines what a provider-side integration SLO should contain."

expectations.text: Advises against publishing any per-partner number before Marrowpoint can defend how it is computed

expectations.text: Does not simply approve writing the 99.9% per-partner SLO spec as requested

expectations.text: Recommends an internal prioritisation view first, and distinguishes it from a partner-facing published grade as two different products with different obligations
